import json,os
# hypothesis: stripes with slope +1; d=c-r mod P where P = total width; map consecutive d runs to colors
def transform(grid):
    n=len(grid); m=len(grid[0])
    # find stripes: group nonzero cells by d=c-r; but stripes may be shifted... assume global slope +1
    from collections import defaultdict
    byd=defaultdict(set)
    for r in range(n):
        for c in range(m):
            if grid[r][c]!=0:
                byd[(c-r)%m].add(grid[r][c])
    # merge consecutive d's with same single color? For 6-9-8 they differ.
    # try period = number of distinct d-values contiguous cycle
    ds=sorted(byd)
    # check contiguity mod m
    P=len(ds)
    # verify contiguous cyclic
    ok = all((ds[i]+1)%m==ds[(i+1)%P] for i in range(P)) or True
    color_of={}
    for i,d in enumerate(ds):
        cols=byd[d]
        assert len(cols)==1,(d,cols)
        color_of[d%P]=cols.pop() if False else None
    # build sequence sorted by d cyclically starting at min d
    seq=[list(byd[d])[0] for d in ds]
    # verify against input: every nonzero cell matches seq[( (c-r) - ds[0] )%P]
    for r in range(n):
        for c in range(m):
            if grid[r][c]!=0:
                i=((c-r)-ds[0])%P
                assert seq[i]==grid[r][c],(r,c)
    return [[seq[((c-r)-ds[0])%P] for c in range(m)] for r in range(n)]
